picks.headline: Major labels call for AI 'slop' songs to be banned from entering charts around the world
picks.excerpt: Sony, Universal and Warner are pushing to disqualify fully AI-generated 'slop' tracks from global charts as tens of thousands of AI songs hit streaming daily, alongside an RIAA/IFPI proposal to label fully- or partly-AI songs in streaming apps. Frames the emerging rules of the road for AI-made music and how disclosure may shape creative practice.
picks.rationale: Fresh (07-29) industry-policy shift that redraws the rules for AI music on charts and streaming labels — high novelty, directly shapes how AI-made tracks compete.

picks.headline: AudioAuditor is a free, open-source audio toolkit with built-in AI music detection
picks.excerpt: AudioAuditor is a free, open-source desktop/CLI player and audio-analysis toolkit that also tries to flag AI-generated music by inspecting watermarks and byte patterns (with the devs candid that detection is still unreliable). A hands-on tool letting producers and listeners probe whether a track was machine-made.
picks.rationale: Most actionable pick — a free, hands-on tool producers can install tomorrow to probe whether audio is AI-generated; distinct from prior BPB coverage.

picks.headline: Only humans can be 'authors', say Canadian music publishers in AI copyright test case
picks.excerpt: Music Publishers Canada has intervened in a court case testing whether AI-generated works qualify for copyright and whether an AI tool can be named a co-author, arguing 'only a human can be an author'. Directly shapes how music creators can claim, protect and credit work made with generative tools.
picks.rationale: Legal test case that directly affects whether and how creators can copyright and credit AI-assisted work — credible, high-stakes, distinct from prior CMU/SOCAN cards.

picks.headline: 'Human-First' is a promise nobody can check yet
picks.excerpt: As 'Human-First' and AI-disclosure labels proliferate across music, this argues they mean little without enforcement, proposing distributor-enforced, open-source-style attestations covering composition, performance, vocals and production. A craft-side look at how AI-use disclosure could actually work for the people making the music.
picks.rationale: Craft-side analysis of how AI-disclosure labels could actually be enforced — practical framing for creators navigating the new labeling push; distinct Hypebot story.
